Trust Fund Operations – Financial Information Summary for the Fiscal years ended June 30, 2024 and 2023

Introduction 1 Trust Funds1 are financial and administrative arrangements made between Development Partners (DPs) and one or more World Bank Group entities to meet diverse development needs including project preparation, technical assistance, advisory services, debt relief, post conflict transition, disaster recovery, climate change, and co-financing of lending projects. Trust funds contribute to the Bank Group’s mission of poverty reduction on a livable planet by supporting the design and implementation of development projects.

This report provides aggregate financial information on trust fund operations administered individually or jointly by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Association (IDA), the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA). These four entities are collectively referred to as the “Bank Group.” This report is unaudited, and is not intended to represent the combined financial position of trust funds and programs administered by the Bank Group. Numbers presented for previous periods have been regrouped to conform to the current period presentation.
Questions or comments on the report should be addressed to Christopher R. Vallyeason, Manager, Trust Funds and Accounting Department at cvallyeason@worldbank.org.

1This report uses the Trust Fund typology of IBRD/IDA Trust Funds, Financial Intermediary Funds (FIFs) and IFC Trust Funds. The following are not included in this report: (1) the Advance Market Commitment (AMC), which is a FIF but not a trust fund, and (2) trust funds that are managed separately by IFC (trust funds which support IFC's Special Initiatives and Investment Programs) which do not form part of the investment portfolio maintained by IBRD for trust funds.

In April 2024, the President announced new financial instruments including the Livable Planet Fund totaling $11,000m that will enable governments, philanthropies and other partner contributions to incentivize cooperation across borders and tackle shared challenges. Japan committed to providing the first contribution to the new Livable Planet Fund.

Ukraine continues to receive support from the international community. New administration agreements have been signed in FY24 for various trust funds supporting Ukraine through SALNTF ($10,167m) and URTF ($661m) programs. Japan and United States were the major donors with expected funding of $7,673m and $2,655m respectively.

During FY24, a new FIF, Global Biodiversity Framework Fund (GBFF) was established. The Trust Fund has been established following the decision of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (“CBD”) at its Fifteenth Session (“COP 15”) to invite GEF to operate the Trust Fund. GBFF aims to support the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Five donors have contributed to-date to this FIF of which, majority of the funding was received from Canada ($55m) and Germany ($44m). TF reforms continued in FY24 with an aim to reduce fragmentation, increase strategic alignment and improve efficiencies of the trust fund portfolio by using fewer and larger Umbrella 2.0 Programs. As of June 30, 2024, 70 Umbrella programs (140 active trust funds) have been established. Four new umbrella programs - EGPS03, DIF, M - GROW and HSTRF have been initiated and activated in FY24.

Commitment authority represents an upper limit up to which task teams can commit future disbursements at the individual TF level. The classes of assets that a trust fund could commit upon form the trust fund’s Basis of Commitment (BoC). The asset classes that can be committed against are either (i) cash, (ii) cash plus promissory notes, or (iii) cash plus promissory notes and contributions receivable. The default BoC for a trust fund is cash, but may be modified to include promissory notes receivable and/or contributions receivable with the approval of Director(s) in the unit managing the trust fund. Cash received from DPs contributions, loans from DPs and proceeds from the issuance of bonds (for IFFIM) are managed by IBRD’s Treasury, which manages a commingled investment portfolio (the Pool) for all funds that are administered by the Bank Group entities. The Pool also includes funds held in ICSID's escrow accounts. IBRD maintains all assets underlying the trust funds’ fund balances separate and apart from the assets of the World Bank Group. IBRD, on behalf of the World Bank Group, invests the funds in liquid financial instruments such as government and agency obligations, time deposits, money-market securities and asset-backed securities, as well as swaps and a range of other derivative instruments. Additionally, the pool may also include equity securities. The investment composition within the pool is based on the investment horizons and cash flow profiles of the trust fund programs. Net investment income earned by the Pool is allocated to each trust fund based on its share of cash and investments in the Pool.
Cash and Investments in DP Balance Accounts

DP balance accounts are established to hold unused funds from closed trust funds, investment income earned on active trust fund balances, or on a temporary basis, subject to separate agreement, funds pending the establishment of another trust fund. The funds in a DP balance accounts may only be returned to the DPs or transferred to other trust funds as a contribution from DPs.
